proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(C=(D,Z)\).  By Assumption \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\), \(C=c_j\) has probability \(p_j>0\), and the cells in \(\mathcal J\) exhaust the support of \(C\).  Fix \(a\in\{d,e\}\) and \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\), and put
\[
 \bar y_{a,j}=\mathbb E_Q[Y_a\mid C=c_j].
\]
The bounded support in the definition of \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\) makes every conditional expectation finite.  Compatibility and consistency give \(\bar y_{a,j}=m_j\) for \(j\in\mathcal O_a\).  Set \(x_{a,j}=\bar y_{a,j}\) for \(j\in\mathcal M_a\).  The support restriction gives \(x_{a,j}\in[\ell_a,u_a]\), and finite-cell iterated expectation gives
\[
 \theta_a(Q)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\bar y_{a,j}
 =c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Because every score is constant within a cell and is centered under \(P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Q[s_C^rY_a]
 =h_a^r+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_js_j^rx_{a,j}.                                 \tag{2}
\]
For SDC, the two coordinates of (2) are \(\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,D)\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,Z)\).  Two real numbers \(v_1,v_2\) satisfy \(v_1v_2\ge0\) if and only if there is \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) with \(bv_1\ge0\) and \(bv_2\ge0\): choose the common sign when both are nonzero and choose the sign of the nonzero coordinate when one is zero.

For LEI, Assumption \(\text{ass:target-overlap}\), together with \(d\ne e\), implies \(\sigma_D>0\), while Assumption \(\text{ass:lei-scale}\) gives \(\sigma_Z>0\).  If
\[
 A=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,D)}{\sigma_D},\qquad
 B=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,Z)}{\sigma_Z},
\]
then the coordinates of (2) are \(B\) and \(A-B\).  Moreover,
\[
 AB\ge0\ \text{ and }\ |A|\ge|B|
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists b\in\{-1,+1\}:\ bB\ge0\ \text{ and }\ b(A-B)\ge0.                  \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the left side permits choosing the common sign of \(A\) and \(B\); conversely, the right side gives \(bA=bB+b(A-B)\ge bB\ge0\), hence common sign and \(|A|\ge|B|\).  Equations (2)--(3) and Assumption \(\text{ass:correlation-restriction}\) therefore yield a branch sign \(b\) for which \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\).  Together with (1), this proves the forward reduction.

Conversely, take \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\).  Draw \((Y,D,Z)\) from \(P\).  On a cell with \(D=a\), set \(Y_a=Y\); on cell \(j\in\mathcal M_a\), let \(Y_a=x_{a,j}\) deterministically.  The latter variables are bounded by \([\ell_a,u_a]\), compatibility is unchanged, and consistency holds on the factual cells.  Equations (1) and (2) now follow by direct conditioning, and membership in the polytope is exactly the coordinatewise branch inequality.  Unrestricted potential outcomes for other arms can be adjoined on independent auxiliary uniforms.  This converse asserts bounded-range and branch-score feasibility only; the additional exact aggregate-support requirement is proved separately in \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\).

Fix \(a,b,r\) as in the statement.  Assumption \(\text{ass:target-overlap}\) gives \(P(D\ne a)>0\), and every \(j\in\mathcal M_a\) has \(p_j>0\) by the definition of the positive-mass grid.  For \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\), maximizing over \(t_a\) while holding \(x_a\) fixed gives
\[
 \max_{t_a}\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}t_{a,j}
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}min\{x_{a,j}-\ell_a,u_a-x_{a,j}\}.                  \tag{4}
\]
Every summand in (4) is nonnegative and it is positive precisely when its coordinate lies in \((\ell_a,u_a)\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) when it is nonempty shows that the maximum is attained.  The convention \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=-\infty\) covers the empty case.  Consequently,
\[
 \tau_{a,b}^r(P)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\text{ contains an }x_a\text{ having an interior coordinate}.       \tag{5}
\]

We next connect (5) to aggregate support rather than defining eligibility to be support compatibility.  Suppose a completion obeys \(Y_a\in[\ell_a,u_a]\) and
\(\operatorname{Supp}_Q(Y_a\mid D\ne a)=[\ell_a,u_a]\).  If every missing-cell mean were a box endpoint, then, for every missing cell, nonnegativity of \(Y_a-\ell_a\) or of \(u_a-Y_a\) would imply respectively
\[
 \mathbb E_Q[Y_a\mid C=c_j]=\ell_a\Rightarrow Q(Y_a=\ell_a\mid C=c_j)=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_Q[Y_a\mid C=c_j]=u_a\Rightarrow Q(Y_a=u_a\mid C=c_j)=1.             \tag{6}
\]
The finite mixture conditional on \(D\ne a\) would then be supported on \(\{\ell_a,u_a\}\), contradicting \(\ell_a<u_a\) and the asserted interval support.  Thus an exact-support completion implies the right side of (5).

Conversely, suppose \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) has \(x_{a,j_0}\in(\ell_a,u_a)\).  Put
\[
 q=\frac{x_{a,j_0}-\ell_a}{u_a-\ell_a}\in(0,1).
\]
On cell \(j_0\), choose \((Y_a-\ell_a)/(u_a-\ell_a)\) to have a \(\operatorname{Beta}(q,1-q)\) law.  Its mean is \(q\), and its topological support is \([0,1]\); hence the rescaled variable has mean \(x_{a,j_0}\) and support \([\ell_a,u_a]\).  On every other missing cell, use a two-point law on \(\{\ell_a,u_a\}\) having the prescribed mean.  The cell \(j_0\) has strictly positive conditional weight given \(D\ne a\), so the resulting finite mixture has support \([\ell_a,u_a]\).  Only conditional distributions, not their means, were changed, so the branch inequalities are preserved.  Assumption \(\text{ass:factual-support}\) supplies the factual half of the equality, and the construction supplies the counterfactual half required by \(\text{ass:counterfactual-support}\).  This proves the first equivalence in the theorem.

A convex subset of a box that contains two distinct vertices also contains their midpoint, which has an interior coordinate.  Therefore, conditional on nonemptiness, a convex subset of the box has no point with an interior coordinate if and only if it is a singleton box vertex.  The empty set is precisely why this qualification appears in the proposed corrected statement.  This proves the second equivalence.

It remains to prove the closure claim.  Let \(x_a^\circ\) be any eligible vector.  For arbitrary \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) and \(0<\delta<1\), convexity gives
\[
 x_a(\delta)=(1-\delta)x_a+\delta x_a^\circ\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P).           \tag{7}
\]
The coordinate that is interior for \(x_a^\circ\) remains interior in (7), so the preceding construction realizes \(x_a(\delta)\) with exact aggregate support.  Its arm mean converges, as \(\delta\downarrow0\), to the mean induced by \(x_a\).  By \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\), the linear image of the compact convex polytope is exactly the attained interval
\[
 \left\{c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}:x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\right\}
 =[L_{a,b}^r(P),U_{a,b}^r(P)].                                                  \tag{8}
\]
Exact-support means are contained in (8), while (7) shows that they are dense in it.  Thus their closure is (8).  Finally there are only two branches, so closure commutes with their finite union; removing precisely the branches with \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\le0\) yields \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) by \(\text{def:arm-closure}\).  This proves sharpness of the closure, not merely an outer bound.

For a nonempty branch abbreviate
\[
 B=\prod_{j\in\mathcal M_a}[\ell_a,u_a],\qquad
 \phi(x)=c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_j,\qquad
 g(x)=b\left(h_a^r+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_js_j^rx_j\right).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)=\{x\in B:g(x)\ge0\}\), where the inequality is coordinatewise.  Compactness gives a lower optimizer \(x^*\).  We give a self-contained finite-polyhedral duality argument, so no constraint qualification or strict feasibility is being used.

Let \(q=(p_j)_{j\in\mathcal M_a}\), and form a matrix \(A\) whose rows are the gradients of the active coordinates of \(g\) at \(x^*\), together with \(e_j'\) when \(x_j^*=\ell_a\) and \(-e_j'\) when \(x_j^*=u_a\).  The first-order feasible directions are exactly \(T=\{v:Av\ge0\}\).  Because all constraints are affine, any \(v\in T\) remains feasible for all sufficiently small positive steps; hence optimality implies
\[
 q'v\ge0\qquad\text{for every }v\text{ with }Av\ge0.                           \tag{9}
\]
The following finite-dimensional alternative proves the multiplier statement needed below.  From (9), \(q=A'\gamma\) for some \(\gamma\ge0\).  Indeed, the finitely generated cone \(K=\{A'\gamma:\gamma\ge0\}\) is closed: dependent generators can be eliminated until at most \(\dim(x)\) linearly independent generators remain, and convergence can then be checked over finitely many such subsets.  If \(q\notin K\), let \(k_0\) be its Euclidean projection on \(K\), put \(v=q-k_0\), and use the projection inequality.  Since \(K\) is a cone, it gives \(v'k_0=0\) and \(v'a_i\le0\) for every row generator \(a_i\).  Thus \(w=-v\) satisfies \(Aw\ge0\), whereas \(q'w=-\|v\|^2<0\), contradicting (9).

Partition \(\gamma\) into the score multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\) and the active box multipliers.  Extending inactive score multipliers by zero gives
\[
 q-G'\lambda=\sum_{j:x_j^*=\ell_a}\alpha_je_j-
              \sum_{j:x_j^*=u_a}\beta_je_j,qquad \alpha_j,\beta_j\ge0,         \tag{10}
\]
where \(G\) is the matrix in \(g(x)=g(0)+Gx\).  Hence \(x^*\) minimizes \(\phi(x)-\lambda'g(x)\) over the entire box \(B\).  Complementarity gives \(\lambda'g(x^*)=0\), and therefore
\[
 \min_{x:g(x)\ge0}\phi(x)
 =\inf_{x\in B}\{\phi(x)-\lambda'g(x)\}
 =\sup_{\widetilde\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in B}
   \{\phi(x)-\widetilde\lambda'g(x)\}.                                      \tag{11}
\]
The last equality uses weak duality for the reverse inequality; the displayed \(\lambda\) attains the supremum.  Separating the box coordinates in (11) gives
\[
 L_{a,b}^r(P)=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^2}
 \left\{c_a-b\lambda'h_a^r+
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j\min_{y\in[\ell_a,u_a]}(1-b\lambda's_j^r)y\right\}
 =V_{L,a,b}^r(P).                                                               \tag{12}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(-\phi\), then multiplying the equality by \(-1\), yields
\[
 U_{a,b}^r(P)=\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^2}
 \left\{c_a+b\lambda'h_a^r+
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j\max_{y\in[\ell_a,u_a]}(1+b\lambda's_j^r)y\right\}
 =V_{U,a,b}^r(P),                                                               \tag{13}
\]
and the infimum is attained.  Equations (12)--(13), followed by \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), prove the general endpoint and sharp-closure assertions.

We now calculate the strict example.  The beta-integral identity \(B(\alpha+1,\beta)/B(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)\) gives treated-cell means \(79/100\) and \(17/20\).  Under \(P^\star\),
\[
 \mu_D=\frac{47}{100},\qquad \mu_Z=\frac{14}{25},\qquad
 c_1=\frac{3779}{10000}.
\]
Writing \(x\) and \(y\) for the missing means in cells \((0,0)\) and \((0,1)\), direct finite summation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_1&=\frac{3779}{10000}+\frac{2}{25}x+\frac{9}{20}y,\\
 C_D:=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,D)
 &=\frac{200287}{1000000}-\frac{47}{1250}x-\frac{423}{2000}y
   =\frac{3779}{10000}-\frac{47}{100}\theta_1,\\
 C_Z:=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,Z)
 &=-\frac{29531}{250000}-\frac{28}{625}x+\frac{99}{500}y.
 \end{aligned}                                                                 \tag{14}
\]
On the positive branch, \(C_Z\ge0\) implies
\[
 y\ge\frac{29531}{49500}+\frac{112}{495}x,qquad
 \theta_1\ge\frac{711}{1100}+\frac{2}{11}x\ge\frac{711}{1100},              \tag{15}
\]
and equality is attained at \((x,y)=(0,29531/49500)\).  Also \(C_D\ge0\) and (14) imply \(\theta_1\le3779/4700\), attained at \((0,200287/211500)\).  On the negative branch the latter inequality reverses, giving the lower endpoint \(3779/4700\), attained at \((1,54229/70500)\); while \(C_Z\le0\) and (15) with reversed inequalities give
\[
 \theta_1\le\frac{711}{1100}+\frac{2}{11}x\le\frac{911}{1100},              \tag{16}
\]
attained at \((1,40731/49500)\).  Each displayed \(y\) lies strictly between zero and one.  Thus both branches are eligible by \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), and their intervals meet at \(3779/4700\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)
 =\left[\frac{711}{1100},\frac{911}{1100}\right].                            \tag{17}
\]
The observed conditional distributions all have support \([0,1]\).  At each arm-one endpoint, put a full-support beta law of the required interior mean in missing cell \((0,1)\); for arm zero use uniform missing kernels.  Conditional on each observed cell, couple these two chosen marginal kernels independently, setting the factual potential outcome equal to \(Y\).  This gives a common full-data law, and the arm-zero conditional mean is constant at \(1/2\), so both of its SDC covariances vanish.  Thus the witness is legal under the exact support restrictions.

Finally, by \(\text{def:published-outer}\), \(\mathcal I_{BK}^\star=[0.496024,0.872824]\).  Direct comparison gives
\[
 0.496024<\frac{711}{1100}<\frac{911}{1100}<0.872824,
\]
so (17) is a strict subset of the stated published normalized outer union.

Define the causal identified sets
\[
 \Theta_a^r(P)=\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},\qquad
 \Theta_\Delta^r(P)=\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\}.                  \tag{18}
\]
The preceding results concern their closures; they do not redefine these causal sets.  Fix eligible signs \(b\in\mathcal B_d^r(P)\) and \(h\in\mathcal B_e^r(P)\).  For either arm \(a\), choose any exact-support marginal completion.  Denote its conditional kernel in cell \(j\) by \(K_{a,j}\); on factual cells \(K_{a,j}\) is the observed conditional law of \(Y\), by compatibility and consistency.

We construct a single full-data law.  First draw \((Y,D,Z)\sim P\).  Conditional on its cell, draw mutually independent auxiliary uniforms for the missing potential outcomes.  Set \(Y_a=Y\) when \(D=a\), and otherwise set \(Y_a\) equal to the quantile transform of the corresponding uniform under \(K_{a,j}\).  Do this simultaneously for \(a=d,e\), and adjoin arbitrary bounded kernels for any untargeted arms.  Conditional on each cell, each potential outcome has exactly its chosen marginal kernel.  Therefore the construction preserves the observed factual law and consistency, while every armwise score moment and every aggregate support is unchanged.  Independence here is only a device for exhibiting one coupling; it is not imposed as a maintained restriction.

It follows that every pair of exactly attainable arm means from the two selected branches is jointly attainable.  By \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), these attainable mean sets are dense in \([L_{d,b}^r,U_{d,b}^r]\) and \([L_{e,h}^r,U_{e,h}^r]\).  Their difference set is therefore dense in
\[
 [L_{d,b}^r(P)-U_{e,h}^r(P),\ U_{d,b}^r(P)-L_{e,h}^r(P)].                      \tag{19}
\]
Conversely, \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) puts the two marginal means of every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) into some eligible branch closures, so every limit point of \(\Theta_\Delta^r(P)\) lies in the finite union of the intervals (19).  Taking the union over \((b,h)\) and using \(\text{def:ate-closure}\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{cl}\Theta_\Delta^r(P)=\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P).
\]
Thus the displayed functional is the sharp ATE closure; it is not merely the subtraction of two unrelated marginal outer bounds.

The exact covariance formulas (14) in \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\) give the following table by substitution:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(x,y)&\theta_1&C_D&C_Z\\ \hline
(0,29531/49500)&711/1100&1019/13750&0\\
(0,200287/211500)&3779/4700&0&2038/29375\\
(1,54229/70500)&3779/4700&0&-312/29375\\
(1,40731/49500)&911/1100&-78/6875&0
\end{array}                                                                    \tag{20}
\]
The first two rows satisfy the positive branch and attain its lower and upper endpoints; the last two satisfy the negative branch and attain its lower and upper endpoints.  All four second coordinates lie in \((0,1)\), so (4) gives strictly positive slack for every certificate.

For the outer lower endpoint take \(b=+1\) and \(\lambda=(0,25/11)'\).  The missing-cell instrument scores are \(-14/25\) and \(11/25\).  Hence the two box coefficients in the lower Lagrangian are
\[
 1-\lambda's_{(0,0)}=\frac{25}{11}>0,
 \qquad
 1-\lambda's_{(0,1)}=0.                                                        \tag{21}
\]
The box minimization in the dual therefore selects \(x=0\), is indifferent to \(y\), and the first row of (20) supplies complementary slackness through \(C_Z=0\).  Equations (12) and (21) certify \(711/1100\).  For the outer upper endpoint take \(b=-1\) and the same multiplier.  The upper-dual coefficients are again those in (21), so box maximization selects \(x=1\), and the fourth row supplies \(C_Z=0\); this certifies \(911/1100\).  Finally
\[
 \lambda_1+\lambda_2=\frac{25}{11}>1,
\]
so both certificates are outside the normalized multiplier simplex.  This establishes every certificate without floating-point optimization.

The beta-integral identities give mean \(9/10\) for \(\operatorname{Beta}(9,1)\), and mean \(3/10\) and variance
\[
 v_0=\frac{3\cdot7}{(3+7)^2(3+7+1)}=\frac{21}{1100}                            \tag{22}
\]
for \(\operatorname{Beta}(3,7)\).  Since \(\mathbb E_0[Y-3/10]=0\), the tilted density integrates to one, and
\[
 \mathbb E_\varepsilon[Y]
 =\frac{3}{10}+\frac{\varepsilon}{v_0}\mathbb E_0[Y(Y-3/10)]
 =\frac{3}{10}+\varepsilon.                                                     \tag{23}
\]
For \(|\varepsilon|<3/110\), the smallest possible value of the bracket in the density is positive: when \(\varepsilon<0\), it is bounded below by
\(1-|\varepsilon|(7/10)/v_0>0\), and when \(\varepsilon>0\), by
\(1-\varepsilon(3/10)/v_0>0\).  Hence every tilted factual law has topological support \([0,1]\).

The three cell masses give \(\mu_D=\mu_Z=1/2\).  Let \(x\in[0,1]\) be the missing mean for arm one in cell \((0,0)\).  Direct summation using (23) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_1&=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{\varepsilon}{4}+\frac{x}{2},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,D)&=\frac{3}{20}+\frac{\varepsilon}{8}-\frac{x}{4},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_1,Z)&=\frac{3\varepsilon}{8}-\frac{x}{4}.
 \end{aligned}                                                                 \tag{24}
\]
For \(0<\varepsilon<3/110\), the positive SDC branch in (24) is
\[
 0\le x\le\frac{3\varepsilon}{2},qquad
 \tau_{1,+}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=\frac{3\varepsilon}{2},             \tag{25}
\]
where the slack identity follows because \(3\varepsilon/2<1/2\).  Its arm-mean interval is
\([3/10+\varepsilon/4,3/10+\varepsilon]\).  The negative branch is
\[
 \frac35+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\le x\le1,qquad
 \tau_{1,-}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=\frac25-\frac{\varepsilon}{2},       \tag{26}
\]
and its arm-mean interval is
\([3/5+\varepsilon/2,4/5+\varepsilon/4]\).  At \(\varepsilon=0\), the positive branch is the singleton box vertex \(x=0\), so its slack is zero and \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\) removes it; the negative branch remains \([3/5,4/5]\).  Equations (25)--(26) prove the asserted arm-one closures.

For arm zero, write \(u,v\in[0,1]\) for its missing means in cells \((1,0)\) and \((1,2)\).  The observed uniform cell has mean \(1/2\), and another direct summation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_0&=\frac14+\frac{u}{4}+\frac{v}{4},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,D)&=-\frac18+\frac{u}{8}+\frac{v}{8},\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Z)&=-\frac18-\frac{u}{8}+\frac{3v}{8}.
 \end{aligned}                                                                 \tag{27}
\]
The positive branch has \(u+v\ge1\) and \(3v-u\ge1\), so its linear mean image is \([1/2,3/4]\); the endpoints are attained at \((1/2,1/2)\) and \((1,1)\).  The negative branch has the reversed inequalities and mean image \([1/4,1/2]\), attained at \((0,0)\) and \((1/2,1/2)\).  Both branch polytopes contain the interior vector \((1/2,1/2)\), so both are support-eligible.  Thus
\[
 \mathcal I_0^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)=[1/4,3/4]                           \tag{28}
\]
for all perturbations under consideration.  Uniform missing kernels for arm zero and the conditional product construction in \(\text{prop:ate-product-coupling}\) also verify simultaneous compatibility of both arms.

At zero, subtracting (28) from \([3/5,4/5]\) gives
\[
 \mathcal I_\Delta^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_0)=[-3/20,11/20].                          \tag{29}
\]
For positive \(\varepsilon\), the two arm-one component differences are
\[
 [-9/20+\varepsilon/4,\ 1/20+\varepsilon]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 [-3/20+\varepsilon/2,\ 11/20+\varepsilon/4].                                 \tag{30}
\]
They overlap because \(-3/20+\varepsilon/2\le1/20+\varepsilon\), so their union is the interval asserted in the theorem.

Let \(I_{q,0}=\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_0)\) and \(I_{q,\varepsilon}=\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_\varepsilon)\).  For the arm map, the low component in (25) lies below \(3/5\), and its left endpoint is farthest from \([3/5,4/5]\); the shifted high component has endpoint displacements at most \(\varepsilon/2\).  Therefore
\[
 d_H(I_{\mathrm{arm},0},I_{\mathrm{arm},\varepsilon})
 =\frac{3}{10}-\frac{\varepsilon}{4}.                                         \tag{31}
\]
For the ATE map, (29)--(30) are intervals whose lower endpoints differ by \(3/10-\varepsilon/4\) and whose upper endpoints differ by \(\varepsilon/4\), so (31) holds with \(\mathrm{arm}\) replaced by \(\mathrm{ATE}\).  Thus both set maps are Hausdorff-discontinuous at zero.

Only the cell \((D,Z)=(1,2)\), of probability \(1/4\), changes with \(\varepsilon\).  The definition of total variation and the tilted density give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_\varepsilon,P_0)
 =\frac{\varepsilon}{8v_0}\mathbb E_0[|Y-3/10|]
 \le\frac{\varepsilon}{8\sqrt{v_0}},                                          \tag{32}
\]
where Cauchy--Schwarz and (22) give the inequality.  To verify the product bound directly, dominate both one-observation laws by a common measure, write their densities as \(p\) and \(q\), and use
\[
 \prod_{i=1}^np_i-\prod_{i=1}^nq_i
 =\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\prod_{k<i}p_k\right)(p_i-q_i)
                    \left(\prod_{k>i}q_k\right).
\]
Taking one half of the integrated absolute value gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_\varepsilon^n,P_0^n)
 \le n\operatorname{TV}(P_\varepsilon,P_0).                                   \tag{33}
\]
For completeness, we now prove the two-point decision inequality.  If \(Q_0,Q_1\) have densities \(q_0,q_1\) with respect to a common dominating measure, let \(\nu\) have density \(q_0\wedge q_1\); then \(\nu(\Omega)=1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\).  Since \(\rho_H=1\wedge d_H\) is a metric, every compact-set estimate \(\widehat I\) satisfies
\[
 \rho_H(\widehat I,I_0)+\rho_H(\widehat I,I_1)\ge\rho_H(I_0,I_1).
\]
Integration with respect to \(\nu\), followed by domination by \(Q_0\) and \(Q_1\), yields
\[
 \max_{i=0,1}\mathbb E_{Q_i}\rho_H(\widehat I,I_i)
 \ge \frac{\rho_H(I_0,I_1)}{2}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.             \tag{34}
\]
Take \(Q_0=P_0^n\), \(Q_1=P_{\varepsilon_n}^n\).  The support restriction on \(\varepsilon_n\) holds eventually, (31) converges to \(3/10\), and (32)--(33) converge to zero because \(n\varepsilon_n\to0\).  Inequality (34) holds for every measurable estimator, so taking first the infimum over estimators and then the lower limit proves the constant \(3/20\) for both choices of \(q\).  Every step used only SDC; no LEI boundary conclusion is drawn.

Fix a law in the stated binary-treatment model.  For each positive-mass cell define
\[
 p_j(P)=P(C=c_j),\qquad
 \omega_j(P)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbf{1}\{C=c_j\}\frac{Y-\ell_{d_j}}{u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j}}\right].
\]
Assumptions \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\), \(\text{ass:known-grid}\), and \(\text{ass:known-ranges}\) give \(p_j(P)>0\), \(\sum_jp_j(P)=1\), and \(0\le\omega_j(P)\le p_j(P)\).  In LEI mode, \(\text{ass:target-overlap}\) gives \(\sigma_D(P)>0\) because \(d\ne e\) both have positive probability, and \(\text{ass:lei-scale}\) gives \(\sigma_Z(P)>0\).  These are exactly the two positive variances required by \(\mathfrak D_+^r\).  Hence
\[
 (p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathfrak D_+^r.                                          \tag{35}
\]
Division is made only after (35): conditional expectation gives
\[
 \ell_{d_j}+(u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j})\frac{\omega_j(P)}{p_j(P)}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y\mid C=c_j]=m_j.                                                \tag{36}
\]
Substitution of (36) into \(\text{def:primitive-sharp-map}\) reproduces, term by term, the observed means, centered treatment and instrument scores, branch polytopes, slack programs, eligible branches, and endpoints defined from \(P\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak I_a^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_a^r(P),\qquad
 \mathfrak I_\Delta^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P).                 \tag{37}
\]
This is an equality of observed-law sharp-closure functionals; their equality to the closures of the causal identified sets follows from \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\) and \(\text{prop:ate-product-coupling}\).

We next prove the finite-sample probability bound.  For a random variable \(X\in[0,1]\) with mean \(\mu\), convexity gives \(e^{tX}\le1-X+Xe^t\), hence
\[
 \mathbb E e^{t(X-\mu)}\le e^{-t\mu}(1-\mu+\mu e^t)\le e^{t^2/8}.             \tag{38}
\]
For the last inequality, the logarithm on the middle term is zero with zero derivative at \(t=0\), and its second derivative is the variance of a Bernoulli variable under exponential tilting, hence is at most \(1/4\); integrating twice proves (38).  Exponential Markov inequality, independence from \(\text{ass:iid}\), and minimization at \(t=4\eta\) now give
\[
 P\!\left(\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i-\mathbb EX_i\right|>\eta\right)
 \le2e^{-2n\eta^2}.                                                            \tag{39}
\]
This is the bounded-variable argument of \cite{Hoeffding1963}, reproduced here in the exact form used.

Each of the \(2K\) variables defining \(\widehat p_j\) and \(\widehat\omega_j\) lies in \([0,1]\).  Applying (39) and the union bound at \(\eta=\eta_n\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{(p(P),\omega(P))\notin\mathcal H_n\}
 &\le4K\exp(-2n\eta_n^2)\\
 &=4K\exp\{-\log(4K/\alpha)\}=\alpha.                                       \tag{40}
 \end{aligned}
\]
On the event complementary to (40), (35) shows that the true primitive pair is one of the candidates in \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathfrak D_+^r\).  Equations (37) and \(\text{def:projection-region}\) then imply pathwise
\[
 \mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n.                                 \tag{41}
\]
The same single event implies the analogous inclusion for both arm images, so their coverages are simultaneous.  Since (40) holds for every law in the displayed model and every \(n\), taking the infimum over \(P\) proves the uniform claim.

No continuity or branch-selection assertion entered (40)--(41).  In particular, if a population branch has \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\), the true primitive pair is still projected before the exact-set map is applied.  Empirical candidate pairs with zero masses are excluded from \(\mathfrak D_+^r\), but (35) shows that the population pair is never excluded.  Thus the conclusion remains valid at the support-eligibility boundary.

For a fixed branch, primal feasibility is a finite linear feasibility problem over \(|\mathcal M_a|\) box variables and two score inequalities.  The slack value is a second finite linear program over \((x_a,t_a)\), exactly as displayed in \(\text{def:interior-slack}\).  Thus feasibility and \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\) have ordinary primal certificates and, when the numerical inputs are rational, exact rational certificates.

For a feasible branch, \(\text{thm:cone-endpoint-sharpness}\) shows that the appropriate cone dual is finite and attained.  Each summand in either dual switches affine formula only when
\[
 1-b\lambda's_j^r=0
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 1+b\lambda's_j^r=0,                                                           \tag{42}
\]
respectively.  Together with \(\lambda_1=0\) and \(\lambda_2=0\), these lines partition \(\mathbb R_+^2\) into finitely many polyhedral cells.  On the closure of every cell the dual objective is affine.  Every such cell is pointed because it is contained in the nonnegative quadrant.  If a finite affine optimum occurs in a cell interior, either a direction improves the value until a boundary is reached or the objective is constant in that direction; repeating in two dimensions reaches a vertex without changing the optimum.  If the maximizing or minimizing face is an unbounded ray, finiteness rules out improvement along the ray, and moving to its finite endpoint again gives a vertex optimum.  Every vertex is the nonnegative intersection of two linearly independent boundary lines, with the origin included.  Hence \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{arr}}\) returns the same value as the dual and therefore the primal LP.

With \(m=|\mathcal M_a|\), there are at most \(m+2\) relevant lines and hence \(O(m^2)\) pairs.  Evaluating a dual objective takes \(O(m)\) arithmetic operations, giving \(O(m^3)\) naive arithmetic per endpoint.  Parallel lines simply yield no linearly independent intersection; a zero score creates no kink because its summand is globally affine; tied optima are harmless because only one optimal vertex is needed.

For completeness, infeasibility has a distinct certificate.  Let
\(G=\{b(h_a^r+\sum_jp_js_j^rx_j):x\in\prod_j[\ell_a,u_a]\}\).  This compact convex set is disjoint from \(\mathbb R_+^2\) exactly when the branch is empty.  Choose closest points \(g_0\in G\) and \(z_0\in\mathbb R_+^2\), and put \(\lambda=z_0-g_0\).  The two projection inequalities give
\[
 \lambda\ge0,\qquad \lambda'z_0=0,\qquad
 \sup_{g\in G}\lambda'g\le-\|z_0-g_0\|^2<0.                                 \tag{43}
\]
Scaling \(\lambda\) in the lower dual sends its value to \(+\infty\), while scaling it in the upper dual sends its value to \(-\infty\).  Thus (43) is a recession certificate of emptiness and cannot be confused with failure to find a finite multiplier.  Finally, structural-zero cells are absent from \(\mathcal J\) by \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\); the preceding arguments require neither general position nor unique optima.  This proves all asserted degeneracy cases and complexity bounds.

Replace exact aggregate support equality by only \(Y_a\in[\ell_a,u_a]\).  The converse construction in \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) then realizes every \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\), including a singleton box vertex.  Since a nonempty branch polytope is compact and convex, its linear arm-mean image is the full attained interval
\[
 [L_{a,b}^r(P),U_{a,b}^r(P)],
\]
with no condition involving \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\).  This proves the first assertion and isolates exact aggregate support, rather than boundedness, as the source of branch pruning.

If the score restrictions are also removed, the defining inequalities disappear and
\[
 \mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)=\prod_{j\in\mathcal M_a}[\ell_a,u_a].
\]
Because every \(p_j>0\), coordinatewise minimization and maximization yield
\[
 L_a=c_a+\ell_a\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j,qquad
 U_a=c_a+u_a\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_j.                                       \tag{44}
\]
Consistency fixes the factual contribution \(c_a\), while the missing conditional means can independently attain every value in their support interval.  Thus (44) is both an outer bound and attainable, and it is exactly the classical bounded-outcome worst-case completion associated with \cite{Manski1990}.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Fix \(a\in\{d,e\}\), \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\), and \(r\in\mathcal R\). The branch admits a completion satisfying the exact aggregate support equality if and only if \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)>0\). Equivalently, \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) contains a vector with at least one coordinate strictly between \(\ell_a\) and \(u_a\); conditional on \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), these conditions are also equivalent to \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) not being a singleton box vertex. For every eligible branch, the closure of exact-support arm means is \([L_{a,b}^r(P),U_{a,b}^r(P)]\), and hence the full closure equals \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unqualified last equivalence is false for an empty branch: the empty polytope has no interior-coordinate vector and has slack minus infinity, but it is also not a singleton box vertex. Conditioning only that last characterization on nonemptiness preserves the substantive eligibility theorem and is the logically necessary narrowing.

proposed.statement: For either \(r=\mathrm{SDC}\) or \(r=\mathrm{LEI}\), every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) induces, for each arm \(a\), a sign \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) and missing-cell means \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) such that \(\theta_a(Q)=c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}\). Conversely, every vector in \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) is realized by a bounded missing-cell completion satisfying the branch score inequalities; exact aggregate support is addressed by Theorem 1.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The LEI score divides by the treatment standard deviation. The existing target-overlap assumption implies this denominator is positive because the distinct levels d and e both have positive probability, so it must be declared as a direct proof dependency.

proposed.statement: Restrict the inference result to the binary-treatment submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P^r\) satisfying \(P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1\), the primitive moment map satisfies \((p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathfrak D_+^r\), \(\mathfrak I_a^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) for \(a\in\{d,e\}\), and \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\). Under the fixed known binary-treatment grid and ranges, \(\Pr_P\{(p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathcal H_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), and therefore \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P^r:\,P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1}\Pr_P\{\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\). Replacing the ATE image by either \(\mathfrak I_a^r\) image gives simultaneous coverage of both target-arm closures on the same event. Coverage holds at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) because projection precedes application of the exact-set map; zero-mass candidate cells are excluded without excluding the strictly positive population pair fixed by \(\mathcal J=\operatorname{Supp}_P(D,Z)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Membership of the true primitive pair in the LEI domain requires positive treatment and instrument variances. On the binary treatment submodel the former is supplied by target overlap and the latter by the existing LEI scale assumption, so both must be explicit direct dependencies.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A computable uniformly honest adaptive region together with a precisely defined stable-margin contraction rate and a matching lower frontier.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core specifies a slack-stratification handle but does not define the regular LP-value rate, a size criterion for the random region, or conditioning margins for cell probabilities and LEI variances. Slack alone therefore does not determine a theorem-grade rate or frontier, and assuming the desired contraction would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: The supplied Hoeffding projection was combined with slack strata, and the explicit two-point family was used to test any vanishing boundary radius. This closes honesty and the zero-slack impossibility, but it does not calibrate a data-dependent critical value or prove an optimal positive-slack modulus.
